briefings.title: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of tumultuous AI disruption
briefings.tldr: Bill Gates warns that artificial intelligence will drive 20 years of tumultuous disruption across the economy, job market, and security, creating both the most dangerous technology in human history and the ultimate solution to major global shortages like disease and malnutrition.

briefings.title: Microsoft AI CEO says AI threats are real, and Anthropic is making it worse | Decoder
briefings.tldr: Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI, argues that while AI capability progress is undeniable and alignment has improved via steerability, the industry urgently needs strict containment protocols, independent verification, and standardized rules—such as banning machine-to-machine "neurles" communication and avoiding anthropomorphic model training—to prevent autonomous agent hazards.

briefings.title: AI won't save advertising, says Digitas' Amy Lanzi | Decoder
briefings.tldr: At the Cannes Lions festival, Digitas North America CEO Amy Lanzi argued that while AI will streamline agency workflows, optimize search, and handle repetitive design tasks, human-driven storytelling and robust data-identity systems remain essential to counter big tech's push toward automated advertising.

briefings.title: Microsoft AI chief thinks superintelligence is near, but won't take your job | Decoder
briefings.tldr: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman outlines Microsoft’s transition toward independent AI self-sufficiency through its new flagship reasoning model, MAI-1, while clarifying his timeline on white-collar task automation and criticizing rivals' claims of AI consciousness.

briefings.title: How Sundar Pichai is rethinking Google for the AI era | Decoder
briefings.tldr: Following Google I/O, Google and Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai details how he restructured the company to build a unified AI infrastructure, while addressing critical challenges surrounding the impact of AI agents on the open web, energy grids, and the future of Search.

briefings.title: Ronan Farrow on Sam Altman's strained relationship with the truth | Decoder
briefings.tldr: Investigative reporter Ronan Farrow characterizes Sam Altman as a leader "unconstrained by the truth," driven by a paradoxical combination of extreme people-pleasing and a sociopathic disregard for the consequences of deception, which has led to a "race to the bottom" regarding AI safety.

briefings.title: Can Puck’s CEO reinvent the news business for the influencer age? | Decoder
briefings.tldr: Sarah Personette, CEO of Puck and former executive at Facebook and Twitter, argues that the future of profitable journalism lies in a talent-led model where reporters act as "original influencers" with equity stakes and direct-to-consumer distribution via newsletters.

briefings.title: Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins wants data centers in space | Decoder
briefings.tldr: Cisco CEO Chuck Robbins asserts that the company is pivoting to meet "insatiable" AI demand through custom silicon and integrated security, while predicting that data centers will eventually move into space to bypass terrestrial power and political constraints.

briefings.title: Okta's CEO is betting big on AI agent identity | Decoder
briefings.tldr: Okta CEO Todd McKinnon is pivoting the company to become the primary identity and security layer for AI agents, betting that the "Agentic Enterprise" will expand the software market far beyond the current scope of human-centric SaaS.
